resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Habitability (resale)
resale_co.issued_by: Wantage Township (historically the zoning/code enforcement office); the current Township site sends resale smoke/CO inspections to the Hardyston Fire Prevention Bureau
requirements: Visual safety inspection (older Township checklist): no work done without permits
Working smoke detectors on each level, including basement and walk-up attic; CO detector in the common area outside bedrooms
Fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, mounted (older checklist still lists it)
Relief valve pipes on water heater and boiler within 6 inches of the floor; handrails/guardrails for more than four steps
Switch and outlet covers in place, no exposed wiring or open boxes, electric panel with no openings; GFIs working where originally installed
Sound stairs, no holes in attached garage walls or ceilings, working toilets and faucets, hot water at least 110 degrees
Proper venting of furnace/boiler and water heater, metal or UL listed foil dryer vents, bathroom ventilation
No broken windows, illegal conversions or illegal living areas; working septic and well/water

resale_co.how_to_apply: The Township's live Forms and Fire Prevention pages link only to the Hardyston Fire Prevention Bureau's online CSACMAPFEC form (Sussex and Wantage) for resales; no current Township Certificate of Habitability application is linked. Call the Zoning Office (973-875-7195, option 7) to confirm whether a separate Continued Certificate of Habitability inspection is still done.

resale_co.notes: Evidence is mixed. The Township Code fee chapter (Chapter 21, read through the ecode360 print view, last amended 5-8-2025 by Ord. No. 2025-12) still lists Certificate of Habitability resale fees of $80/$85/$150, and a Township PDF checklist (file dated 2014) says a Continued Certificate of Habitability is required on all re-sales. But no Code section creating the requirement was found in Chapter 8 (Building and Housing) or the Board of Health chapters, the checklist and an old COH form are no longer linked on the live Forms page (the COH form link returns 404), and the live site sends resale smoke/CO inspections to the Hardyston Fire Prevention Bureau. Neighboring Sussex Borough has moved its resale Certificate of Habitability to Hardyston, and Wantage may have done the same. Note the Code's first fee tier ($80) is lower than the middle tier ($85) as written. Rental units need a Certificate of Registration ($80 per unit) and Board of Health septic/water certificates (Chapter BH10); those are rental-only.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area (NFPA 72); hardwired interconnected alarms from construction must stay that way
10-year sealed battery smoke alarms (ANSI/UL 217); A/C powered alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarms (UL 2034) in the immediate vicinity of sleeping areas where there is a fuel-burning device or attached garage
Secondary power source warning label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter if the home has a permanent generator, solar panels or battery storage
All construction permits must be closed with the Construction Department
No portable fire extinguisher is required

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply and pay online through the Hardyston Fire Prevention Bureau portal (Sussex and Wantage - CSACMAPFEC form), linked from Wantage's Fire Prevention and Forms pages. A representative contacts you to schedule within a few business days. Paper applications are at the Hardyston Township Municipal Building Construction Office window, 149 Wheatsworth Road. Online payments add a processing fee.

fire_cert.notes: Hardyston's posted rules say a portable fire extinguisher is no longer required, in line with P.L.2025, c.19, even though the older Wantage checklist lists one. The fee and schedule text comes from Hardyston's online payment page (Tyler portal), which is built with JavaScript, so a script may not read it; the same rules also appear in Hardyston's regulations PDF. The Wantage construction office is also run by Hardyston under a shared service agreement (checks payable to Hardyston Township; construction@hardyston.com, 973-875-7195 option 6).

other_items.label: Open construction permits
other_items.detail: All construction permits must be closed with the Construction Department before the smoke/CO certificate. Wantage's construction office is run by Hardyston Township under a shared service agreement (973-875-7195 option 6, construction@hardyston.com).

open_questions: Does Wantage still require a separate Continued Certificate of Habitability inspection for resales, or is the Hardyston smoke/CO certificate now the only Township item?
If a Certificate of Habitability is still required, who inspects, what form is used, and are the Code fees ($80/$85/$150) still charged?
Is a septic or well certification required by the Township at sale (the Board of Health chapter covers rentals only)?
